out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: while responding to question about cooling of cooked cauliflower, the food employee touched the cauliflower with a bare hand.
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. The EHS discussed this with the PIC and the PIC discussed it with the food employee.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Cover Foods in Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped or uncovered food in the following location where the food is subject to contamination: lamb curry and garlic sauce were stored uncovered in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Foods shall be protected from contamination by being stored in packages, covered containers or wrappings unless being cooled. Unless being cooled, all foods stored in the walk-in must be covered to prevent contamination. The PIC has this corrected during the inspection.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked chicken, black lentils, lamb curry and tikka Marsala were not being held cold enough in the walk-in at 46º, 48º, 49º, and 50º,=.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The foods were discarded.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. There was an unlabeled chemical spray bottle on the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. The PIC labeled the bottle during the inspection. BANSARI INDIAN CUISINE (Inspection Date: 09/03/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: in standing room temperature water on the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. Discontinue thawing foods in standing water.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: at the bar, the ice scoop handle was stored in the ice for making drinks.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The food employee corrected this during the inspection by moving the ice scoop handle.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: the ambient temperature of the walk-in was 51º and foods in it were not being held cold enough.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Have the walk-in serviced as soon as possible. Contact your EHS when it is adjusted or repaired and keeping foods cold enough again.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Air Gaps/Breaks
violations.observation: The diameter of the air gap between the water supply inlet (sprayer hose) and the flood level rim of the three compartment sink is less than twice the diameter of the water supply inlet.
violations.corrective_action: An air gap between the water supply inlet and the flood level rim of the plumbing fixture, equipment, or nonfood equipment shall be at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet and may not be less than one inch. Correct as soon as possible or within 3 days.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: DOK Clean and Sanitize
violations.observation: There is no certified food manager on duty and the person in charge failed to explain the correct procedures for cleaning and sanitizing utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment. No one was able to properly describe how equipment and utensils are supposed to be washed rinsed and sanitized at the three compartment sink. Also, there was no bleach or other sanitizer present in the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall know that all utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be 1) washed with hot, soapy water to remove visible soil, 2) rinsed to remove residue, 3) sanitized using an approved sanitizer to reduce the number of bacteria and viruses and 4) air dried. The EHS educated the staff on how to properly set up the 3-compartment sink.

violations.title: DOK Time and Temp Req
violations.observation: There is no certified food manager on duty and the person in charge failed to state the required temperatures and holding times for the time/temperature control for safety food items when (1) in refrigerated storage, (2) in hot holding, (3) being cooled and/or (4) being reheated. No one was able to state how foods should be cooled properly.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall know the following: 1) Cold foods shall be stored at 41F or below, 2) Hot foods shall be held at 135F or above, 3) Foods for cooling shall be rapidly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F or below within a total of 6 hours, and 4) Foods shall be reheated to an internal temperature of above 165F if prepared on site or above 135F if commercially processed. All foods must be cooled properly at all times. The EHS discussed proper cooling with the chef/food employee.

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the permit to operate in a conspicuous location. The 2025 (not 2026) permit was posted on a wall but obscured by other documents placed over it.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. Post the 2026 health department permit in a conspicuous location within 10 days.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' The PIC was not able to provide the employee health policy for the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. The EHS provided all food employees with the model FCHD employee health policy. Staff read and completed the forms during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS provided the manager with a copy of the model FCHD policy which they will adopt. CDI.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of equipment at being cleaned at. The 3-compartment sink were not observed sanitized. There was no bleach available or other sanitizer available on site.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. The staff obtained bleach from another location during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Four large covered plastic bus pans of black lentils (2) and garbanzo beans (2) cooked yesterday were 75º, 69º, 70º, and 67º in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. The EHS discussed proper cooling practices with the chef. The four containers of product were discarded due to improper cooling. CDI.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Discard Food when Exceeds 4 Hours
violations.observation: During a discussion with one of the food employees, it was learned that food such as cooked chicken and cauliflower which are on TPHC, were not being discarded at the end of the four hour limit.
violations.corrective_action: Food being held as time only (no temperature controls) must be discarded after the four hour limit is reached and may not be refrigerated or served. The EHS discussed this with the food employees. CDI. BANSARI INDIAN CUISINE (Inspection Date: 03/10/2026) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Containers of cleaning chemicals were stored over the ice machine opening.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. This was corrected during the inspection by moving the chemicals. CDI.

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. There were several unlabeled spray bottles of cleaning solution in the dining room and in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. Staff labeled the unlabeled bottles during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: cooked foods (lentils and garbanzo beans) made yesterday were placed in large, plastic covered bus pans, which are not suitable for rapid cooling. Several other were stored in the same covered containers but made several days ago. Foods can’t cool properly stored that way.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Foods must be broken down into smaller portions and containers and uncovered to cool, and cooled within 6 hours, otherwise, they will have to be discarded. Correct within 10 days.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Two containers of tandoori chicken were stored under the prep table and on the floor next to the oven.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. The food employee moved the chicken to the refrigerator during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. Correct within 10 days.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: in-use utensils were stored in water that was 94º.
violations.corrective_action: Utensils can be stored in water, but the water must be at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The food employee corrected this during the inspection. CDI. BANSARI INDIAN CUISINE (Inspection Date: 03/10/2026) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed a rack of clean glasses stored under the table in dish washing machine room. Observed clean pots stored on the floor in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Cleaned equipment and utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items shall be stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches off the floor on NSF approved shelving units or dunnage racks. All food equipment must be stored off the floor. Correct as soon as possible or within 90 days.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers including numerous 5-gallon yogurt buckets, were observed reused for the storage of hot and cold foods.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. Remove all reused food containers as soon as possible or within 90 days.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): storing food in, storing hot pots in (these milk crates were badly melted, deteriorated and not clean), keeping food equipment off the floor, stored equipment and utensils..
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. MILK CRATES ARE NOT APPROVED FOR ANY REUSE IN A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. REMOVE ALL MILK CRATES AS SOON AS POSSIBLE OR WITHIN 10 DAYS.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: large spice containers such as black pepper, red pepper and others were being reused to store other foods.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers such as spice containers and 5-gallons buckets are not designed or approved for being re-used in a food establishment to store other foods. They must be discarded or removed from the establishment when emptied and not used to store other foods such as raisins and fennel, as observed today. Remove all reused food containers as soon as possible or within 90 days.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the low temperature, chemical sanitizing warewashing machine was observed with a sanitizing rinse concentration of less than 50 ppm chlorine solution.
violations.corrective_action: Immediately discontinue use of the dishmachine. Until the machine is adequately repaired, set up the three-compartment sink to manually wash, rinse and sanitize food-contact surfaces using a sanitizing solution at the proper concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine.
